claims.explanation: Repaglinide is a meglitinide insulin secretagogue that closes ATP-sensitive potassium channels by binding the SUR1/KCNJ11-ABCC8 complex, and this same KATP channel activity can influence cancer cell survival and proliferation. Selectivity is most plausibly explained by expression of the drug's targets (ABCC8, KCNJ11) and by transporters such as SLCO1B1/SLCO2B1 that determine intracellular exposure, with PPARG expression providing an additional context-dependent sensitizing or protective influence. Lines lacking the target channel complex or with high efflux/transport-mediated clearance would be protected.

features.basis: Target of repaglinide; KATP channel closure can trigger apoptosis in cells expressing the channel
SUR1 subunit target of repaglinide; required for KATP channel drug response
Annotated repaglinide target; PPARG signaling can modulate proliferation and apoptosis
OATP1B1 transporter can mediate hepatic uptake and intracellular exposure of substrate drugs
OATP2B1 transporter can mediate drug uptake and increase intracellular exposure
OATP1A2 can mediate drug transport at the blood-brain barrier and other tissues
CYP2C8 metabolism can inactivate drugs; high expression may reduce active drug levels
Efflux transporter expression can lower intracellular drug concentration and reduce killing
Damaging mutations in the KATP channel target could abolish repaglinide binding and response
Loss-of-function SUR1 mutations can prevent KATP channel closure by repaglinide
